sections.name: ThemeToggle
sections.title: Light, dark and system theme switch
sections.what: Shows three small icon buttons for light, dark, and system themes. The selected one is highlighted. Until the page has loaded in the browser, it shows a blank pulsing bar instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: the current theme is only known in the browser, so waiting for the page to load avoids a mismatch between server and browser output.
sections.watch_out: The three theme names used by the buttons must match the names the theme library accepts, or the buttons will do nothing.

summary: Three small icon buttons (light, dark, system) that switch the app between light, dark and device-based color themes.
purpose: Lets the user choose how the app looks and shows which choice is active.
why: Likely reason: the saved theme is only known in the browser, so a flag waits until the component is on screen before showing the real buttons. The code does not state this.
how: On first render it shows a plain placeholder box. After the component mounts in the browser, the flag is set and the three buttons appear. Each button calls setTheme with its name. The active button is highlighted using the current theme value.
inputs: The current theme and the setTheme function, both supplied by the next-themes library.
outputs: A visible theme change in the app, and a highlighted button for the active theme.
risks: Depends on a theme provider from next-themes being present higher up in the app, which is not visible here. Without it the buttons may do nothing.
debug: If the buttons do nothing, check that the app wraps its pages with the next-themes provider. If the placeholder never turns into buttons, check that the mounting effect runs.
